tasks.task: Write a full business plan from the owner's facts

items.when: When you have the owner's accounts, costs and notes and need a structured plan for each reader
Before writing, to get the business on nine blocks and see gaps between customers and costs
When the market section needs sourced facts and sizing that shows its assumptions
When the plan needs three years of revenue, costs and cash with scenarios
When the draft is done, to find every claim a lender or panel would want a source for

tasks.task: Put the whole business on one page

items.when: Before a full plan, or as its summary, to share with a partner, mentor or bank
When the owner thinks in boxes, not prose, and a canvas version would be clearer
When a long plan exists and the page must give the answer first with the numbers
When the page lists activity and never says who the customer is or what to stop

tasks.task: Prepare a bank loan application and lender plan

items.when: When the owner wants a loan or grant and needs the steps from eligibility to a sent file
When the plan must be re-cut for a lender with funding request, use of funds and repayment
When the lender asks how the next 90 days of cash look and what the risks are
Before applying, to test whether the loan can still be repaid in a bad year
Before the file goes in, to list missing documents, expiry dates and open questions

tasks.task: Prepare a small business grant application

items.when: When a council, government or foundation grant is open and the steps need setting out
Before spending time on it, to get a go or no-go call on whether the grant fits
When the funder's rules are known and the answers must match them point by point
Before sending, to tie every fact in the application to a dated source
After the award, when the funder wants spending reconciled with evidence

tasks.task: Check a draft plan before it goes to a bank or panel

items.when: When a draft plan is about to go to a bank, a grant panel or a partner
When money is about to be committed, to get the strongest case against the plan
Before a lender meeting, to face tough questions with a suggested answer to each
When you are too close to the draft and need it read fresh, as the lender would
When the plan has one outcome that could ruin the owner and no answer to it

tasks.task: Research the market and rivals for the plan

items.when: When the plan needs a market size built from the bottom up with guesses marked
When you have facts on a rival and need their prices and strengths set against the client's
When the research must stand alone as a sourced report a lender can check

tasks.task: Work out start-up costs and break-even

items.when: Before committing money to a new business, site or product line, to see cost to open
When prices and costs are set, to see break-even volume and the margin of safety
When break-even looks comfortable, to test how big a loss a bad first year brings
When the owner plans to spend a lot before anyone has paid for anything

tasks.task: Build the plan's financial projections

items.when: When a new business needs revenue, costs and cash for three years with scenarios
When the business has trading history and the forecast should start from past numbers
When the model is built, to find which assumptions break first and what to test
Before the workbook is shared, to catch formula errors and totals that do not tie

tasks.task: Test a business idea before spending on it

items.when: When there is only an idea and it needs a tested customer, a position and a price
When several kinds of buyer might want it, to compare groups and pick one to talk to
When the riskiest guess needs a test planned and its result read honestly
When the owner keeps planning and has not yet asked one person to pay

tasks.task: Build a dated set-up checklist for a new business

items.when: When someone is starting or has just started and wants set-up done in order
When you need each set-up step with its official page, owner and deadline
When the structure is undecided, to compare options on risk, tax and paperwork
When nobody has listed the risks, the usual cover and what may be required
When the owner is leaving a job and needs the monthly income they must reach first

tasks.task: Plan the first employee, from cost to start date

items.when: When the first hire is planned and each legal step needs an owner and a deadline
Before the offer, to flag whether the work looks like employment or contracting
When a start date is set and payroll needs a dated set-up plan and questions
When the owner knows the problem to fix but has no job description yet

tasks.task: Work out a day rate and hourly rate

items.when: When a freelancer needs minimum and target rates from income, costs and billable hours
When you want the rate cross-checked from target pay, costs and billable hours
When the rate is known and you need a fee, billing terms and a cap on one client
When the freelancer has traded a while, to see each client's real rate per hour

tasks.task: Shape services into three packages with clear limits

items.when: When services are sold by the hour and need three packages with scope and limits
Before you fix the packages, to draft a three-tier ladder and compare
When a package needs a name, value framing, a guarantee and payment terms
When the packages are drafted, to score each and get the three changes that matter

tasks.task: Write a quote or proposal for a client project

items.when: When a brief arrives and the freelancer needs scope, price assumptions and terms
When one price feels like take it or leave it, to offer three options instead
When the quote must become a proposal or statement of work with the right clauses
Before sending, to have the quote read fresh as the client would read it
When the client later asks for more and the change must be priced against the scope

tasks.task: Build a contract checklist and lawyer questions

items.when: Before a first client contract goes out, terms change, or the client's paper is signed
When the client sends their own contract, to rate key clauses and duties by risk
When there is no contract at all and a first draft is needed for the lawyer to review

tasks.task: Set up the client process and message templates

items.when: When clients get lost between first call and paid invoice, or every message is written fresh
When new enquiries arrive and each needs qualifying and a first reply
After a first call, to turn notes into a follow-up email and next steps
When a job is won and needs a one-page brief and a clear start
When clients message on every channel and need set channels and update dates
Before a template is saved, to score it and cut what the client will not read

tasks.task: Invoice clients and chase late payment

items.when: When work is done and an invoice needs the right details with totals added
Before sending, to recalculate every line and find missing fields
When an invoice is late, to get a warm reminder and a firm follow-up to choose from
When several invoices are open and someone must decide who to chase each week

tasks.task: Build a 13-week cash forecast

items.when: When you have bank statements, invoices and bills and need the lowest week and days of cash
When sales are seasonal and the owner needs a downside case and a buffer
When an earlier forecast exists, to see how far it missed what really happened
When a lean stretch is likely and the owner needs a buffer rule and who to ask early

tasks.task: Set up profit-first allocation and the routine

items.when: When sales are steady but little is left and the owner needs target percentages by account
When the percentages are set and the twice-monthly routine and quarterly check must run
When the accountant has quoted a tax share and each payment needs a rule and a place
Each month, to sort transactions and check them against the allocation targets
When profit on paper and cash in the bank disagree and the owner asks why

tasks.task: Sort worries into accountant, lawyer or do it yourself

items.when: When an owner has a list of worries and needs to know which professional to ask and how
When one decision has tax effects and the owner needs facts and questions for a tax pro
When the worry is the structure itself and options need comparing before the meeting
When the worry is a contract and the lawyer needs the risky clauses listed first

tasks.task: Plan how to win the first customers

items.when: When the business is new and the first customers must be won one by one
When the plan needs a simple marketing page from stranger to loyal customer
When the owner targets everyone, to compare groups and choose where to start

tasks.task: Check the business is ready for a second site

items.when: Before signing a second lease, to see if the first site runs without the owner
When the second site needs its own opening costs and break-even worked out
When the first site works only because the owner is there every day

always.when: Before anything goes to a bank, panel or client, to find claims with no source
Before the owner reads it, to find finance and legal jargon and put it in plain words

helpers.when: When the books are behind and the plan or forecast has no clean numbers to start from
When the owner faces debt, a lender problem or a big money decision beyond set-up
When rates and packages need buyer evidence, rival prices or a price test
When the first hire needs a contract, policies or a fair hiring process
When the grant is large or competitive and needs a full funder-matched bid
When the plan needs a real local marketing plan, not one page

gaps: No library item writes a full small business plan for a lender or grant panel; the nearest items plan venture-style startups
No library item writes the lender section: funding request, use of funds, security offered and ability to repay
No library item finds or checks eligibility for small business grants; grant items serve nonprofits and research
No library item lists start-up costs or builds an opening budget; only break-even is covered
No library item builds a country-specific business registration checklist linked to official pages
No library item covers the first hire beyond payroll: contract, right to work checks, pension and employer insurance
No library item sets profit-first target percentages, an account structure or an allocation day worksheet
No library item builds a 13-week cash forecast by week; the cash forecast item works in 30, 60 and 90 day blocks
No library item maps a service firm's client process from enquiry to paid invoice or writes the full set of client messages
No library item offers different tones of client message to compare, such as warm, brief and formal
No library item lists what a first freelance client contract must contain; contract items review an existing one
No library item writes a rate rise notice for a freelancer's existing clients
No library item prepares an owner for a meeting with a bank manager
